title: Eureka residents expected to return home Thursday days after Iron Fire forces evacuation
text:
Eureka residents are expected to return home on ThursdayAfter days of shelters, trailers, and homes of relatives, Eureka residents will be allowed home tomorro
A human-caused wildfire has burned thousands of acres in north Juab County near Eureka, sending thick smoke into the sky. After days of staying in shelters, trailers, and with friends or family, Eureka residents are expected to be able to return home on Thursday.
“We’re looking at getting you guys home tomorrow,” said Juab County Sheriff Travis Kenison to the crowd at Apple Valley Elementary. But the threat of the Iron Fire isn’t completely gone, so the town will still be in SET status. Although many are happy to be able to go back, that threat is keeping some, like Leslie and Wayne Rice, from going back right away.
“I think there will be a number of people like us that have seen how protections don’t necessarily work all the time, that want to wait until after the winds this weekend,” Leslie Rice said. For those who do want to get back into their homes right away, they’ll have to enter town from the west because Hwy 6 will still be closed for a few days. But just the ability to get home is enough for some.
“I see some people that are handicapped and are down at the shelter, and they’re kind of frustrated they can’t get back up there, so this will be a break for them to be able to get back home,” Wayne Rice said. Officials said there will be fire resources in town for the next several days and nights to make sure everyone and everything in town is as safe as possible.
The Cottonwood Fire burning near Beaver quickly grew to an estimated 31,000 acres with zero percent containment, according to Utah fire officials late Tuesday. The Iron Fire burning near Eurkea grew to 37,172 acres after making a run east through the Pinyon Canyon area, Utah fire officials said Wednesday morning.
